Build with UIForge

UIForge is a reusable UI component library built from scratch using HTML, Vanilla JavaScript, and SCSS/Sass. It provides reusable UI components, responsive layouts, CSS utilities, consistent styling, and reusable component classes.

UIForge was built to understand how UI libraries work internally while creating a reusable library that can be used across web projects.

View Components GitHub

Quick Start

Step 1 — Include UIForge

Use UIForge directly through the public CDN without copying the source files into your project. Add the UIForge stylesheet inside the <head> of your HTML file.

HTML 
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@diksha2004/uiforge@1.1.0/dist/uiforge.css">
HTML 
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
  <title>UIForge Example</title>

  <link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@diksha2004/uiforge@1.1.0/dist/uiforge.css">
</head>
<body>

</body>
</html>

Step 2 — Use UIForge Classes

After including the stylesheet, use UIForge classes directly in your HTML. UIForge components are used by adding their predefined classes to HTML elements.

HTML 
<button class="btn btn-primary">
  Primary Button
</button>

Cards use the real component structure provided by UIForge: the card stylesheet styles nested headings and paragraphs directly.

HTML 
<div class="card">
  <h3>Hello UIForge</h3>
  <p>
    Build interfaces using reusable UIForge classes.
  </p>
</div>

Hello UIForge

Build interfaces using reusable UIForge classes.

Step 3 — Responsive Layout

UIForge provides responsive layout classes so you can create flexible layouts without writing the basic responsive CSS yourself.

HTML 
<div class="container">
  <div class="row">
    <div class="col-12 col-md-6">
      Content
    </div>

    <div class="col-12 col-md-6">
      Content
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
Content
Content

Step 4 — Components

UIForge includes reusable buttons, cards, alerts, badges, navbars, avatars, forms, dropdowns, pagination, and tabs. Explore the existing component documentation to see each component in detail.

Explore Components

Step 5 — Utilities

UIForge also provides utility classes for common spacing, display, flexbox, sizing, color, typography, and border needs. For example, combine d-flex, gap-2, and p-2 to arrange and space content.

HTML 
<div class="d-flex gap-2 p-2">
  <span>Spaced content</span>
  <span class="fw-bold">Emphasized content</span>
</div>

Installation

CDN

No npm installation is required for a simple HTML project. The stylesheet is loaded from jsDelivr, and the version is pinned explicitly to @diksha2004/uiforge@1.0.0 for predictable usage.

HTML 
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@diksha2004/uiforge@1.0.0/dist/uiforge.css">

npm

Install the package with npm when you want the distributed stylesheet available in your project. For plain HTML, the CDN method above is the recommended documented quick-start method.

Bash 
npm install @diksha2004/uiforge

Complete Example

This example uses the published stylesheet and verified UIForge classes from start to finish.

HTML 
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">

  <title>UIForge Example</title>

  <link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@diksha2004/uiforge@1.0.0/dist/uiforge.css">
</head>

<body>

  <div class="container">
    <h1>My UIForge Page</h1>

    <button class="btn btn-primary">
      Get Started
    </button>
  </div>

</body>
</html>

UIForge Documentation

A reusable CSS library for building clean, modern interfaces.

UIForge is a lightweight CSS component library built with semantic HTML, structured SCSS, and simple Vanilla JavaScript patterns for fast, consistent UI development.

Built with

HTML, Vanilla JavaScript, SCSS/Sass, and Vite — designed to stay lightweight and easy to use.

Getting Started

Learn how to run UIForge locally and use its components in your projects.

1. Project Setup

Clone or open the repository, then install the project dependencies via npm:

Bash 
npm install

2. Available npm Scripts

The following npm scripts are defined in package.json:

Command Description
npm run dev Starts the Vite local development server with Hot Module Replacement (HMR).
npm run build Compiles SCSS and bundles JavaScript for production into the dist/ directory.
npm run preview Locally previews the production build created in dist/.

3. Basic Usage

To use UIForge components, link the compiled stylesheet (or import src/scss/main.scss in your bundler) and use the semantic component classes:

HTML 
<!-- Button example -->
<button type="button" class="btn btn-primary">Get Started</button>

<!-- Alert example -->
<div class="alert alert-success">Action completed successfully!</div>

Design Tokens: Typography

Typography tokens for font family, scale, weights, line heights, and letter spacings.

Base Font Family: $font-family-base: 'Plus Jakarta Sans', system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif;

Font Sizes ($font-sizes)

Token Value Utility Class Sample
$font-size-sm 0.875rem (14px) .text-sm Small readable copy
$font-size-base 1rem (16px) .text-base Standard body paragraph
$font-size-lg 1.125rem (18px) .text-lg Subheadings and lead text
$font-size-xl 1.5rem (24px) .text-xl Section headings
$font-size-2xl 2rem (32px) .text-2xl Page Titles (H1)

Font Weights ($font-weights)

Token Value Utility Class
$font-weight-regular400.fw-regular
$font-weight-medium500.fw-medium
$font-weight-semibold600.fw-semibold
$font-weight-bold700.fw-bold

Line Heights & Letter Spacings

Category Tokens Values Utility Classes
Line Heights $line-height-tight, $line-height-normal, $line-height-relaxed 1.25, 1.5, 1.75 .lh-tight, .lh-normal, .lh-relaxed
Letter Spacings $letter-spacing-tight, $letter-spacing-normal, $letter-spacing-wide -0.025em, 0, 0.025em .ls-tight, .ls-normal, .ls-wide

Design Tokens: Spacing Scale

The spacing system uses the Sass map $spacings. Access values in SCSS with map.get($spacings, key).

1 0.25rem (4px)
2 0.5rem (8px)
3 1.0rem (16px)
4 1.5rem (24px)
5 2.0rem (32px)
Map Syntax Rule

Do not write $spacing-1 or $spacing-2. In SCSS, always use: map.get(variables.$spacings, 2) or map-get($spacings, 2).

Design Tokens: Radius

Generic border radii and component-specific organic radii.

Token Value Purpose
$radius-sm0.25rem (4px)Small elements, tags, input checkboxes
$radius-md0.5rem (8px)Dropdown menus, inputs, pagination buttons
$radius-lg0.75rem (12px)Cards, forms, navbar, tab containers
$radius-full999pxCircular avatars, pills, switch toggles
$radius-button0.35rem 0.9rem 0.35rem 0.9remDistinctive asymmetric UIForge button corners
$radius-badge0.3rem 0.8rem 0.3rem 0.8remDistinctive asymmetric UIForge badge corners

Design Tokens: Borders, Motion & Focus

Border specifications, interaction timing, and accessible focus rings.

Category Tokens Values Description
Border Widths $border-width-thin, $border-width-medium, $border-width-thick 1px, 2px, 3px Standardized line weights for borders and dividers
Border Styles $border-style-solid, $border-style-dashed, $border-style-dotted solid, dashed, dotted Standard border line styles
Motion / Transition $transition-duration-base, $transition-easing-base 160ms, ease Micro-interaction timing for hover and press states
Focus Indicator $focus-width, $focus-color, $focus-offset 2px, $brand-400 (#818cf8), 2px High-contrast accessible focus ring for keyboard navigation

Design Tokens: Breakpoints & Fluid Foundations

Mobile-first em-based scale respecting user browser font-size settings, fluid clamp() tokens, and container max widths.

Breakpoint Token Min-Width (em scale) Container Max-Width Typical Purpose
sm36em (~576px)33.75rem (540px)Large phones/landscape, 2-up cards
md48em (~768px)45rem (720px)Tablets, navbar expands, forms go multi-col
lg62em (~992px)60rem (960px)Laptops, full layout, sidebars
xl75em (~1200px)71.25rem (1140px)Wide desktops, container max-width
xxl87.5em (~1400px)82.5rem (1320px)Ultra-wide displays

Centralized SCSS Responsive Mixin

Breakpoints are stored in one SCSS map and accessed via the shared up($breakpoint) mixin. Components never use hardcoded numbers.

SCSS 
@use "variables";

.my-component {
  // Mobile-first default: single column, stacked
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;

  // Tablet & above: expand layout
  @include variables.up(md) {
    flex-direction: row;
  }
}

Intrinsic Fluid Tokens

UIForge provides fluid tokens using CSS clamp() so typography and spacing scale smoothly without requiring media queries on every element:

CSS Variable Formula Purpose
--uf-font-size-h1clamp(1.85rem, 1.25rem + 2.5vw, 3rem)Fluid hero & page title typography
--uf-space-sectionclamp(2rem, 5vw, 4.5rem)Fluid vertical section spacing
--uf-gutterclamp(1rem, 3vw, 1.5rem)Fluid container & grid gutters
--uf-container-max1280pxDefault container content cap

Responsive Buttons & Button Groups

Full-width block buttons, mobile-only block buttons (.btn-block-sm), and wrapping button groups.

Viewport Test:
HTML 
<!-- Button group that wraps cleanly on mobile -->
<div class="btn-group">
  <button type="button" class="btn btn-primary">Save Changes</button>
  <button type="button" class="btn btn-secondary">Cancel</button>
  <button type="button" class="btn btn-white">Export Data</button>
</div>

<!-- Full width on mobile, auto-width above 576px -->
<button type="button" class="btn btn-primary btn-block-sm">Mobile Block</button>

<!-- Always full width -->
<button type="button" class="btn btn-black btn-block">Full Width Block</button>
ClassDescription
.btnBase button with 44px min tap target, padding, asymmetric radius, and hover-gated elevation.
.btn-blockFull-width button across all viewports (width: 100%).
.btn-block-smFull-width on mobile screens (<576px), auto-width on tablet and desktop.
.btn-groupFlexbox wrapper with flex-wrap: wrap that prevents horizontal row blowouts.
.btn-primaryPrimary action color using $brand-500.
.btn-secondarySecondary muted action color using $secondary.
.btn-success, .btn-dangerSemantic confirmation and destructive action styles.
.btn-warning, .btn-infoCaution and informative action styles.
.btn-black, .btn-whiteHigh-contrast monochrome button variants.

Container Query Horizontal Card (.card-horizontal)

Uses @container card (min-width: 28rem). On narrow containers (mobile or sidebar) it stacks vertically. When its container has 28rem+ width, it shifts to horizontal layout automatically without viewport media queries!

Container Width:
16:9 Responsive Media
CONTAINER QUERY

Adaptive Card Architecture

This card responds to its parent's width, not the device viewport. Test toggling between Full and 375px above.

Zero Viewport Queries

Alert Variants

Use .alert with semantic modifiers.

Your profile was updated successfully!
Data sync completed with all endpoints.
Unable to reach authentication server. Please retry.
Warning: This action cannot be undone.

<div class="alert alert-primary">Your profile was updated successfully!</div>

Dismissible Alert with Action Group

Features top-aligned status icon, content wrapper, reachable 44px dismiss button, and wrapping action buttons.

Storage Limit Warning

Forms & Validation

Form controls, labels, text inputs, textareas, selects, custom checkboxes, radio controls, switches, and validation states.

Form Controls & Validation States

A complete form example showing common controls and validation states.

Account Registration

Enter your details to create your account.

Email format is valid and verified.
Username cannot contain spaces or symbols.
HTML 
<form class="form">
  <h3 class="form-title">Account Registration</h3>

  <p class="form-description">
    Enter your details to create your account.
  </p>

  <div class="form-group">
    <label class="form-label" for="doc-form-name">
      Full Name
    </label>
    <input
      class="form-input"
      id="doc-form-name"
      type="text"
      placeholder="John Doe"
    >
  </div>

  <div class="form-group">
    <label class="form-label" for="doc-form-email">
      Email (Valid)
    </label>
    <input
      class="form-input is-valid"
      id="doc-form-email"
      type="email"
      value="alex@example.com"
    >
    <div class="valid-feedback">
      Email format is valid and verified.
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="form-group">
    <label class="form-label" for="doc-form-user">
      Username (Invalid)
    </label>
    <input
      class="form-input is-invalid"
      id="doc-form-user"
      type="text"
      value="invalid user name!"
    >
    <div class="invalid-feedback">
      Username cannot contain spaces or symbols.
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="form-group">
    <label class="form-label" for="doc-form-message">
      Message
    </label>
    <textarea
      class="form-textarea"
      id="doc-form-message"
      placeholder="Write your message..."
    ></textarea>
  </div>

  <div class="form-group">
    <label class="form-label" for="doc-form-plan">
      Subscription Plan
    </label>
    <select class="form-select" id="doc-form-plan">
      <option value="">Select a plan</option>
      <option value="starter">Starter Plan</option>
      <option value="pro">Pro Developer</option>
      <option value="team">Team Edition</option>
    </select>
  </div>

  <div class="form-group">
    <label class="form-check">
      <input
        class="form-check-input"
        type="checkbox"
        checked
      >
      <span class="form-check-label">
        I agree to the Terms of Service
      </span>
    </label>
  </div>

  <div class="form-group">
    <label class="form-check">
      <input
        class="form-check-input"
        type="radio"
        name="account-type"
        checked
      >
      <span class="form-check-label">
        Personal account
      </span>
    </label>

    <label class="form-check">
      <input
        class="form-check-input"
        type="radio"
        name="account-type"
      >
      <span class="form-check-label">
        Business account
      </span>
    </label>
  </div>

  <div class="form-group">
    <label class="form-switch">
      <input
        class="form-switch-input"
        type="checkbox"
        checked
      >
      <span class="form-check-label">
        Enable email notifications
      </span>
    </label>
  </div>

  <div class="form-actions">
    <button type="reset" class="btn btn-secondary">
      Reset
    </button>

    <button type="submit" class="btn btn-primary">
      Submit Form
    </button>
  </div>
</form>

Tabbed Interface

Switch panels by clicking or using left/right keyboard arrows when focused.

Semantic HTML5 provides the structural backbone with standard accessible WAI-ARIA roles.

SCSS Tokens define a centralized map of colors, typography, spacing scales, and transitions.

Vanilla JavaScript enables lightweight, accessible DOM manipulation with zero external runtime dependencies.

HTML 
<div class="tabs" role="region" aria-label="Component preview tabs">
  <div class="tabs-nav" role="tablist">
    <button type="button" class="tab-btn is-active" role="tab" aria-selected="true" aria-controls="panel-1" data-tab-target="#panel-1">HTML</button>
    <button type="button" class="tab-btn" role="tab" aria-selected="false" aria-controls="panel-2" data-tab-target="#panel-2">SCSS</button>

  <div class="tabs-content">
    <div id="panel-1" class="tab-panel is-active" role="tabpanel">HTML Content</div>
    <div id="panel-2" class="tab-panel" role="tabpanel" aria-hidden="true">SCSS Content</div>
  </div>
</div>

Scrollable Multi-Item Tabs

When tab items exceed viewport width, the tab list scrolls horizontally with touch momentum and scroll-snap (scroll-snap-type: x proximity). Active tabs automatically center into view without messy multi-line wrapping.

Preview Width:

Overview content: components scale intrinsically across viewports.

Components content: robust primitives designed for real-world space constraints.

Tokens content: centralized fluid scales using clamp() and em-based breakpoints.

Accessibility: WCAG 2.2 AA compliant, 44px tap targets, 200% zoom reflow.

Architecture: mobile-first SCSS with intrinsic flex and grid layouts.

Changelog: version 1.0.0 responsive standard upgrade complete.

HTML 
<!-- Horizontally scrollable tabs with touch momentum and scroll-snap -->
<div class="tabs" role="region" aria-label="Navigation Tabs">
  <div class="tabs-nav" role="tablist">
    <button type="button" class="tab-btn is-active" role="tab" aria-selected="true">Overview</button>
    <button type="button" class="tab-btn" role="tab" aria-selected="false">Components</button>
    <button type="button" class="tab-btn" role="tab" aria-selected="false">Design Tokens</button>
    <button type="button" class="tab-btn" role="tab" aria-selected="false">Accessibility</button>
  </div>
  <div class="tabs-content">
    <!-- tab panels -->
  </div>
</div>

Grid System

12-column responsive flexbox layout system with breakpoint-specific column span classes.

12-Column Responsive Layout

Columns automatically stack on mobile screens (100% width) and divide according to span at md and larger breakpoints.

Preview Width:
col-12 col-md-4
col-12 col-md-4
col-12 col-md-4
col-12 col-md-6
col-12 col-md-6
HTML 
<div class="container">
  <div class="row">
    <div class="col-12 col-md-4">Column 1</div>
    <div class="col-12 col-md-4">Column 2</div>
    <div class="col-12 col-md-4">Column 3</div>
  </div>
</div>

Intrinsic Auto-Fit Grid (Zero Media Queries)

Uses modern CSS Grid repeat(auto-fit, minmax(min(100%, 16rem), 1fr)) to automatically create 1, 2, 3, or 4 columns based on available container width without any viewport media queries.

Auto Item 2

<div class="grid-auto-fit">
  <div class="card">...</div>
  <div class="card">...</div>
  <div class="card">...</div>
</div>

Utilities

Atomic utility classes generated dynamically from design tokens and mobile-first breakpoint loops.

Category Classes Example Usage
Responsive Display .d-none, .d-block, .d-flex, .d-grid
.d-{sm|md|lg|xl}-{none|block|inline|flex|grid} 		<div class="d-none d-md-flex">...</div>
Responsive Flex .flex-row, .flex-column, .flex-wrap
.flex-{sm|md|lg|xl}-{row|column|wrap|nowrap}
.justify-{sm|md|lg|xl}-{start|center|end|between}
.align-{sm|md|lg|xl}-{start|center|end} 		<div class="flex-column flex-md-row">...</div>
Responsive Text .text-{sm|md|lg|xl}-{left|center|right} <p class="text-center text-md-left">...</p>
Accessibility .visually-hidden
.visually-hidden-focusable 		<span class="visually-hidden">Skip to content</span>
Fluid Spacing .section-space (fluid clamp(1.5rem, 5vw, 4rem) padding)
.m-{1-5}, .p-{1-5}, .gap-{1-5} 		<section class="section-space">...</section>
Overflow Container .overflow-x-auto (accessible horizontal scroll wrapper for tables/code) <div class="overflow-x-auto"><table>...</table></div>
Colors .text-primary, .text-secondary, .text-success, .text-danger
.bg-primary, .bg-neutral-100, .bg-neutral-900 		<p class="text-primary bg-neutral-100">...</p>
Typography .text-sm, .text-base, .text-lg, .text-xl, .text-2xl
.fw-regular, .fw-medium, .fw-semibold, .fw-bold 		<h2 class="text-xl fw-bold">...</h2>
